text:
maria_support: Heads up — Customer ACME (prod) reporting intermittent 401s when calling /v1/generate. Error from our side: "invalid_signature". Happening ~5% of requests, mostly from eu-west nodes. Ticket #INC-4821.

josh_security: Thanks. Any commonalities? region, model, header payload?

maria_support: They paste logs:
```
HTTP 401 {"error":"invalid_signature","reason":"kid not found"}
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <JWT>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Tokens are minted by ACME's IdP (third-party). They said IdP rotated keys ~10m ago.

kevin_infra: If kid not found, that usually means our JWKS cache still has old keys or cached a JWKS that didn't include the new kid. What TTL do we set for jwks fetch?

josh_security: Our runtime caches JWKS per issuer for 5m by default and also respects Cache-Control headers from the IdP. But there are two additional layers: CDN (edge cache) and our local in-memory cache on each inference node. If the IdP rotated and returned a JWKS missing the old kid during a short window, verification might fail until a full refresh.

elaine_sre: Also saw a pattern where some tokens verify fine on us-east but fail on eu-west. Could be inconsistent propagation of new keys or clock skew on customer side. We should check node times as well.

maria_support: Customer confirms their clock is NTP-synced. They also say failures started immediately after IdP rotation and lasted ~8 minutes.

josh_security: Repro suggestion: try to fetch the JWKS during the window when their IdP rotates and compare responses from different regions/nodes. Use curl with --resolve to hit specific edges. Example:
```
# hit eu-west edge
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:3.120.45.11 "https://api.redwood.ai/.well-known/jwks.json"
```
Compare the jwks JSON. Also dump Cache-Control and TTL headers.

kevin_infra: I pulled logs: our edge returned jwks.json with `cache-control: public, max-age=300` from the IdP originally. But a downstream CDN response for eu-west had `age: 580` due to upstream propagation delay — so some edges were serving an older JWKS for ~10m. That fits.

josh_security: Two problems in combination: 1) IdP rotation removed the old kid before all tokens expired, 2) our distributed caches/CDN caused stale/partial view of keys. Also some of our verification libs reject tokens if `kid` absent even if you could try all keys (some libs only trust kid header).

maria_support: Customer is asking for mitigation ASAP — they want tokens to be accepted during rollout window.

elaine_sre: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Retry logic: on 401 invalid_signature where kid not found, fetch JWKS from origin (bypass CDN) and retry verification once; 2) Add leeway for clock skew (but that won't help kid mismatch); 3) On key rotation, attempt full JWKS fetch and fallback to try all keys.

josh_security: Agreed. Action plan:
- Short-term (hotfix): implement a hot retry path in verifier: on invalid_signature/kid-not-found -> synchronous JWKS refresh from IdP origin (bypass caches) and re-verify once. Also log metadata (issuer, kid, node, region).
- Medium-term: improve cache invalidation: on 401 with kid mismatch, trigger background refresh for that issuer and optionally purge CDN cache for jwks endpoint if TTL suggests dangerous staleness.
- Long-term: add a verification fallback that loops through all keys when kid lookup fails (but careful: potential security/clock tradeoffs). Also document recommended IdP rotation patterns (publish new key, wait for TTL window, then retire old key).

kevin_infra: I can wire a bypass call to origin via a dedicated internal endpoint that ignores CDN caches. If we do hot-retry we should rate-limit these bypasses to avoid a stampede.

maria_support: Customer also asked about clock skew — they saw a couple of `token_expired` when their servers were 2 minutes ahead. Can we add leeway?

josh_security: We already have a default leeway of 60s in validator. RFC 7519 suggests some leeway. We can increase to 120s for tokens coming from known partners behind a trust relationship, but don't want to widen universally. Suggest adding configurable leeway per issuer.

elaine_sre: Ops note — one node in eu-west had its system clock 4 minutes slow (ntp drift) last night during a deploy. I will patch NTP config and add monitoring alert for host clock drift >30s.

maria_support: Customers want rollback guidance: if they rotate again and see issues, what should they do immediately?

josh_security: Tell them: 1) Publish new key to JWKS and keep old key present for at least JWKS_TTL + token_max_age + 60s (safety margin). 2) If they must remove keys earlier, coordinate with us so we can purge caches and trigger refreshes. 3) Prefer using `kid` and not rotating `alg` at same time.

kevin_infra: Implementing hot-retry now on a branch. Patch will: on verifier error type kid-not-found OR invalid_signature with matching issuer->kid header, do a blocking GET to IdP origin (bypass cache header: Cache-Control: no-cache, Pragma: no-cache) and re-run verify. Rate-limit 10/s per issuer per region. Log full jwks sizes and response headers.

elaine_sre: I'll add host clock drift alert, and we'll run a one-off sweep of eu-west nodes for NTP status.

maria_support: I'll update ACME support ticket with mitigation steps and ask them to preserve old key for 15m on next rotation.

oauth-bot: Deployment pipeline: created PR #1027 (eng/security) for hot-retry. Staging run scheduled.

josh_security: Thanks all. Post-mortem items: operational docs for idp rotations, cache invalidation playbook, per-issuer leeway config, and telemetry to correlate jwks fetches with 401 spikes. Assigning owners: kevin -> cache bypass + rate-limit; elaine -> clock monitoring; maria -> customer comms; josh -> verifier fallback and docs.

maria_support: Customer replied: thanks, will coordinate next rotation. Marking incident resolved for now but keeping follow-ups open.

kevin_infra: Deployed hotfix to staging; will test by simulating rapid key rotation against staging jwks and hitting different edges.

josh_security: Add unit tests: simulate missing kid in header, ensure we do the bypass-refresh then reverify, and that we don't fallback to accepting tokens without valid signature.

elaine_sre: I'll schedule a 1h runbook review next Tue to ensure oncall knows steps.

maria_support: Closing loop with ACME now. Thanks team :tada:
